# Fixed-fan two-sided support lineality and centroid-hull reversal

This note refines, rather than reproves as new, the finite support cone in
`candidate 94a1565e143d393e`. The new specialization is
an exact reversal criterion and a strict-quota example in which every
individual reversed support function is valid, but an active anchored
inequality immediately forbids the reversed family. There is no assertion
of a polytopal minimizer, density of stationary polytopes, or OC payment.

## 1. The actual finite support cone

Let P be a finite lattice-complete base set and let all sampled fibers be
positive-dimensional polytopes in R^d. Fix a complete simplicial fan F
refining all their normal fans. Write its rays as u_r and its maximal
cones as sigma. For a support array h=(h_zr), define

    v_z,sigma = U_sigma^(-1) h_z,sigma,

where the rows of U_sigma are the ray vectors of sigma. Use the following
finite linear inequalities:

    C_z,sigma,r(h) = h_zr - u_r . v_z,sigma >= 0,       (1)
    B_q,lambda,r(h) = h_qr - sum_z lambda_z h_zr >= 0.  (2)

Here lambda ranges over the vertices of the anchored representation
polytope {lambda>=0: sum lambda=1, sum lambda z=q}; the trivial delta_q
representation can be omitted. Stack (1)--(2) as A h>=0.

These are inequalities for ACTUAL support values, not merely offsets in a
possibly redundant halfspace presentation. Indeed (1) says every linear
piece u.v_z,sigma lies below the piecewise-linear function at each ray,
and hence throughout every fan cone. On its own cone it agrees. Thus that
function is the support function of conv{v_z,sigma}. Conversely convexity
of a support function gives (1). Condition (2) on the rays gives the full
support inequality on each cone, hence the corresponding Minkowski
inclusion. Extreme representations suffice by linearity in lambda.

## 2. Exact two-sided lineality, with a turnover qualification

Fix an actual positive array h and let I={a: A_a h=0}. The exact one-sided
radial tangent cone and two-sided first-velocity space are respectively

    {v: A_I v>=0},             E_h={v: A_I v=0}.       (3)

For sufficiency, h+t v satisfies every old active row with the required
sign; all inactive rows retain positive slack for sufficiently small t.
Positivity of the fibers is open. For necessity, apply an active linear
row to h(t)=h+t v+o(t). If this path is defined for both signs of t, the
two signs force equality. Thus every v in E_h has an EXACT two-sided affine
realization, and every differentiable two-sided path in this fixed cone
has velocity in E_h. This is the explicit lineality consequence of the
archived support-cone theorem.

This does not prohibit higher-order facet turnover. For v in E_h,

    h(t)=h+t v+(t^2/2) w

is feasible for both signs near zero precisely when A_I w>=0 (apart from
identically zero rows); inactive rows remain harmless. Thus an old zero
bend can open at second order. For example, adjoin the ray (1,1) to the
four cardinal rays of the square [-1,1]^2. Its support value is 2. Cutting
with x+y<=2-t creates a new facet for t>0, but for t<0 that inequality is
redundant: the ACTUAL diagonal support is min(2,2-t), which is not
differentiable at zero. In contrast the cut x+y<=2-t^2 is a genuine
two-sided differentiable support path with zero first speed and facet
birth at second order. Treating the raw redundant offset as support would
incorrectly miss this distinction.

All claims here stay on the specified fixed fan. Motions rotating normal
directions outside that fan are not described by (3).

## 3. A complete centroid-hull reverse criterion

More generally let K and D be two compatible polytope families with
D_z subset K_z, and let h,d be their support arrays on a common simplicial
fan. (The compatible centroid hull is one such D.) The forward contraction
(1-t)h+t d is feasible for 0<=t<=1. The reversed candidate is

    h_rev(s)=(1+s)h-s d,             s>=0.             (4)

It is an actual compatible family for some interval 0<=s<=s_0, s_0>0,
if and only if

    A_a d=0 whenever A_a h=0.                          (5)

Equivalently, d belongs to the minimal face of the combined support cone
containing h. Necessity follows from A_a h_rev=-s A_a d on active rows;
both h,d are feasible so A_a d>=0. Sufficiency follows from the finite
inactive slacks. The exact maximal allowed extent is

    s_* = min_{a: A_a d>A_a h} A_a h/(A_a d-A_a h),    (6)

with the minimum of the empty set interpreted as infinity. Equation (4)
is feasible exactly for 0<=s<=s_*. Any realized reverse fiber remains
positive: D_z subset K_z gives h_rev>=h pointwise and hence K_rev contains
K. Formula (6) consequently needs no separate degeneration cutoff.

The criterion has two distinct components. Individual support convexity
requires h_Dz to be linear on every normal cone of K_z, equivalently that
the normal fan of K_z refine that of D_z. To see necessity, on such a cone
h_K is linear; if (1+s)h_K-s h_D is convex, h_D must be both concave and
convex there. Sufficiency is the vanishing of precisely the corresponding
active convexity rows. Lower-dimensional D_z cause no problem. The second
component says EVERY tight anchored K support inequality is also tight
for D. Individual reverse feasibility does not imply this contact rule.

## 4. The old obstruction and a pure-contact refinement

The planar example in
`candidate 6a7efe79d654e5de`
has an upward anchored violation under reversal. Its middle trapezoid
also fails the individual condition in Section 3: its centroid-hull
segment has a normal-fan wall not present in the trapezoid fan. Thus that
example should not be described as isolating the anchored obstruction.

Here is an exact variant which does isolate it. Take P={-1,0,1}, with

    K_- = K_+ = A=[-1,1] x [-3,0],
    K_0 = conv{(-2,0),(2,0),(2,-1),(1,-3),(-1,-3),(-2,-1)}.

The middle contains A, so the family is compatible and its canonical
fiber hull has exactly these three sampled fibers. Direct integration
gives

    |A|=6, g_A=(0,-3/2), |K_0|=10, g_0=(0,-4/3).      (7)

For example the middle widths are 4 on [-1,0] and t+5 on [-3,-1]; its
vertical first moment is -40/3. The total mass is 22 and k(P)=2. Every
proper closed minor has strict mass quota: singleton masses 6,10,6 are
strictly less than 11, while each adjacent-pair mass is 16<22.

The centroid hull has point fibers D_-=D_+={(0,-3/2)} and

    D_0={0} x [-3/2,-4/3].                             (8)

Every individual reversed fiber exists for ALL s>=0. The endpoints are
the homothetic expansions of A by factor 1+s around its centroid. The
middle reversed support is realized by the hexagon with vertices

    ( +/-2(1+s), 4s/3 ),
    ( +/-2(1+s), -1+s/2 ),
    ( +/-(1+s), -3-3s/2 ).                             (9)

Their cyclic order is the one inherited from K_0. The vertical side
length is 1+5s/6>0; the other sides scale by 1+s. Checking the six normal
rays (0,1),(1,0),(2,-1),(0,-1),(-2,-1),(-1,0) shows exactly
h_(9)=(1+s)h_K0-s h_D0. Thus no individual support-convexity defect is
present.

Nevertheless the old upward anchored row has K gap zero and D gap 1/6.
In (9) the middle top is 4s/3, whereas each reversed endpoint top is
3s/2. Hence

    h_K0,rev(0,1) - [h_K-,rev(0,1)+h_K+,rev(0,1)]/2
        = -s/6 < 0.                                  (10)

The family is incompatible for EVERY s>0, even though every constituent
support function is valid for all s. The exact obstruction is one active
anchored inequality. No deepestness or stationary-minimum claim is made.

## 5. Scope and checks

The finite cone itself is archived. The useful additions are the explicit
minimal-face/maximum-step reversal criterion, the first-versus-second
order turnover distinction, and the strict-quota pure-contact example.
They give a test of any proposed reverse centroid-hull deformation; they
do not supply a universally feasible reverse motion.

The companion checker is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_fixed_fan_lineality_and_centroid_reversal_defect_transport.py`.
